scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Healing Sound of the Jingle Dress
This is Jingle Dress Dance. c. 1900.
on_screen: Title card: Jingle Dress Dance · USA · c. 1900

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated around 1900 in Ojibwe communities following a dream by a Midewinini.
It was created as a healing ritual for an ill child and spread from the Mille Lacs and White Earth reservations to the Lakota in the 1920s.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a healing ceremony.
It is performed at powwows, where people may offer tobacco to dancers to request prayers for the sick.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Pow Wow Trail ｜ S1, Ep 07 ｜ Docu-series (https://archive.org/details/youtube-CHRha0H1YPg)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Traditional style features light, grounded footwork without crossing feet or turning circles.
Contemporary style incorporates more complex footwork, including crossing feet, turning, and backward movement.
Watch for Traditional Step.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Danced within a powwow circle.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is driven by the drum and singing.
Dancers must keep time with the beat and stop exactly when the music ends.
Listen for the Drum, Voice.
The music is defined by a steady, driving drum beat and vocal chanting, punctuated by the rhythmic, metallic jingling of the dress cones.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Must follow the drum beat.
scenes.music: the music brief's underscore at its own tempo; drop narration under the hook of a verified recording if licensed, else original

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The regalia consists of a dress adorned with metal cones (historically from tobacco lids).
Modern dresses may use 365 cones to represent the days of the year.
Dancers often carry a feather fan.
on_screen: Image gallery: 4 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variations exist between the traditional style (grounded, no crossing) and the contemporary style (fancier footwork, spins).
Ojibwe origin, spread to Lakota and other tribes.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Jingle Dress Dance is shares music of Men's Fancy Dance: Both are powwow dances that require strict adherence to the drum beat.
on_screen: Graph: the connections with their relation labels

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is a healing ceremony with spiritual origins; it should be approached with respect for its role in prayer and community health.
